1: On examination, there was a 4 × 4 cm area of swelling just left of the natal cleft at the level of the tip of the coccyx, with mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin but no fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits.
2: Given a high suspicion for abscess, percutaneous aspiration was performed in clinic but no fluid was obtained.
3: The differential diagnosis at this time included inclusion cyst and soft-tissue tumor.

A complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass was excised from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx, with a rim of healthy tissue; the mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter.
4: The differential diagnosis at this time included inclusion cyst and soft-tissue tumor.
